issue.title: Retire sase-core's unweighted running_agent_slot_count and is_runner_slot_occupying_record
issue.description:
Proposed by phase sase-1om.5 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1) of epic sase-1om. The plan
told that phase to record it, not change it.

## Proposal

Retire the unweighted Rust occupancy helpers `is_runner_slot_occupying_record` and
`running_agent_slot_count` in `crates/sase_core/src/agent_runtime.rs` of the linked
sase-core repo (`sase repo open sase-core`). At sase-core 16a3ed0 they have no non-test
callers. The weighted `runner_capacity` snapshot (claims, `occupied_lanes`, and per-record
`accounting`) now answers every occupancy question. The Python
`running_agent_slot_count` (src/sase/core/runner_slots/_admission.py) already delegates
to the Rust snapshot. Delete the Rust copies and their tests, or fold any unique
assertions into `runner_capacity/tests/`. Python's own `is_runner_slot_occupying_record`
is still used by `sase agent list` visibility; the related bug task about queued monitor
follow-ups moves that caller to snapshot accounting. Retire the Python predicate there,
or here once that lands.

## Why out of scope

Epic sase-1om's list-holder-parity phase explicitly forbade changing these helpers. It
asked for a follow-up note instead, so the cleanup was never part of the epic's phases.
